criteria.text: `slowGet` rejects once the response's declared `content-length` exceeds `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`, without reading any of the body.

`slowGet` rejects once the accumulated bytes of a response with no (or an understated) `content-length` exceed `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` while streaming, and never resolves a partial/truncated body in that case.

`http.ts` exposes the byte-over-limit decision as a pure, network-free unit, callable directly with synthetic byte counts (no socket, no `fetch`), so its accept/reject boundary is unit-tested without a server.

`gkg.ts`'s `download` checks the zip response's `content-length` against `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` before touching the body, and resolves `{ status: 'oversize', stage: 'compressed', bytes, limit }` when it is over, without calling `res.arrayBuffer()`/reading the stream.

`gkg.ts`'s decompression is bounded by `MAX_EXPANDED_BYTES` (`256 * 1024 * 1024`), enforced while streaming through fflate's `Unzip`, and this bound is exercised by an exported, network-free unit a test can drive with a synthetically built zip (e.g. via `fflate`'s own `zipSync`) to prove both a payload under the limit resolving `ok` with the correct decoded text, and a payload whose decompressed size crosses a (test-injected, small) limit resolving `{ status: 'oversize', stage: 'expanded' }`.
`download` still returns `{ status: 'missing' }` for a 404, unchanged from today's `null`-for-404 behaviour, and an empty zip still resolves `{ status: 'ok', csv: '' }`.

`processSlot` inserts into `gkg_files` only on `{ status: 'ok' }`; on `{ status: 'oversize' }` it logs the stage, the observed bytes and the limit, returns `[]`, and performs no `gkg_files` insert for that slot.

`gkg()`'s slot loop (`sequential(pending, processSlot)`) completes and returns the docs of every non-oversize slot even when one slot in the batch resolves oversize — an oversize result never throws out of `processSlot`.

`rss.ts`'s `fetchFeed` performs the same `content-length` preflight and streaming byte cap against `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES` (imported from `http.ts`, not a re-declared literal) before `res.arrayBuffer()`.

`src/collectors/gdelt.ts`, `src/collectors/camara.ts`, `src/collectors/senado.ts` are unchanged by this issue (verified by diff/review) and their existing test suites (`collectors-senado.test.ts`, `senado-independent-acceptance.test.ts`, `camara-acceptance.test.ts`, `bluesky-timeout.test.ts` insofar as it documents the shared 45 s ceiling) stay green.

`docsText` (across `README.md` and `docs/*.md` together, per `test/docs.ts`) states the 32 MB and 256 MB figures and the fact that an oversized GKG slot is skipped without being marked done, so it is retried on a later run. (`test/docs-drift.test.ts`'s existing collector-registry checks already cover `gkg`'s row in the source table and its filter-value documentation; this issue adds no new source, so no new criterion is needed there.)
`pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` are both green.
